How strictly the scan filters terrain columns for ore quality. This does not predict the material mix excavators will produce.
Off: include all tiles, dig to full depth.
Low: exclude very sparse tiles, trim thin trailing ore at the bottom.
Med: moderate quality — skip tiles with heavy overburden or little ore.
High: only rich tiles with a clean ore column.
Max: apply the strictest overburden, depth, and ore-density filters.

Choose what Create Designations scans for.

AUTO:
• If terrain designations already exist, preserve them and use unfinished terrain-work clusters as pathfinding starts. When an eligible unstarted mine control tower ghost exists, its entrance replaces the active tower as the pathfinding target.
• Otherwise, use an eligible tower ghost as a natural accessway marker and commit the first valid route. A recognized ghost suppresses the product scan even when no route can be placed.
• If neither terrain work nor an eligible ghost exists, scan for useful products and generate their mining plan.

AUTO never falls back to debris or dirt. Select Dirt explicitly, or use the debris-clearance button, when that work is wanted.
Show a striped overlay on terrain ATD predicts may be affected by collapse from live Mining designations. Visible only while the game's terrain designation overlay is shown.

Ignore isolated ultra-thin ore spikes that extend far below the surrounding deposit when creating Mining Designations. This correction runs before Ore quality and bottom flattening. Raw terrain and existing designations are unchanged.

Avoid ocean in generated accessways and mining plans in this world. Mining cells that overlap ocean are excluded. Projected cutting below sea level is also avoided; dumping into ocean remains allowed. Turn this off to allow risky shoreline work.

Avoid buildings in generated accessways and mining plans in this world. Mining cells that overlap a building or its safety perimeter are excluded. Projected terrain disturbance near buildings is also avoided.

Use a background thread for access and mining planning. Enabled by default. Turn off for compatibility troubleshooting; planning then runs on the game thread and may cause pauses, especially in large mines. Applies to new planning requests.

When the full access snapshot is too large for the memory ceiling, try one smaller geometry-only corridor around the current starts and goals. This aims to find some route; it may differ from a full-area route, and failure does not prove that no route exists.

Mark trees in finalized accessway and mining-designation disturbance zones for harvest. When disabled, ATD creates no tree harvest orders. Harvest orders placed by ATD are removed by either Clear action; unrelated player harvest orders are preserved.

Allow debris removal to make the smallest workable terrain change when a prop cannot be excavated without landscaping. When disabled, the removal request fails and the requesting workflow is notified.

Controls when ATD uses the game's Quick remove action for routed accessway debris. Quick remove spends Unity only when the game is unpaused. This policy does not apply to the mine-tower Clear debris button.
Use Quick remove for all accessway debris except props that the planned dumping designation will sufficiently bury. This speeds up landscaping but spends Unity.
Prefer normal excavation but use Quick remove when excavation cannot guarantee post-work pathability.
Never spend Unity on Quick remove for accessway debris. Removal relies on excavation and the Landscape to remove debris setting, and may need the player to provide Quick remove assistance.

If an accessway search exhausts the available routes inside a tower area, retry within 16 tiles beyond its boundary. This fallback applies to both narrow and T3/Mega accessways, does not run after a timeout or other search interruption, and may trigger the game's normal outside-area alarm. Default: enabled.

Controls how cautiously ATD predicts landslides and how much distance it keeps from protected oceans and buildings. Higher policies reserve more space; lower policies allow terrain work closer to hazards. Default: BAL.

Tile-distance cost assigned to one unit of landscaping cost. One landscaping-cost unit is equivalent to dumping or digging one unit of rock. Range: 0-100; default: 1. A higher value promotes routes with less terraforming.

Landscaping cost charged once per prop cleanup origin used by access search. One unit equals one dumped or dug rock unit; default 8 reflects observed excavator cleanup effort. Higher values make cleanup routes less attractive.

Horizontal exclusion distance per vertical terrain level. 1 translates to a 45-degree slope; higher values widen the exclusion zone (use in e.g. pure sand), while lower values narrow it. Range: 0.05-2; default: 1.

Choose what assigned trucks do when this tower has no pending excavation work, or while the tower is paused.

Vanilla behavior: keep trucks assigned and send them back to the tower when idle.
Pros: trucks stay close and ready for the next job.
Cons: idle trucks can occupy the tower area and make unnecessary return trips.

Keep trucks assigned without sending them back to the tower when idle.
Pros: avoids unnecessary return trips and keeps trucks near their last work area.
Cons: trucks may be scattered across the work area.

Temporarily unassign idle trucks so they can assist with general hauling and construction jobs. Trucks are simply re-assigned to this tower when excavation work returns.
Pros: released trucks can help with general hauling and construction while idle.
Cons: if assigned to another tower, especially one not using Soft release, they may be unavailable when this tower's work resumes.
